title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering & token/event framing for OpenAI-compat streaming
author: Avery Chen
description: Fix a class of SSE streaming bugs that caused malformed partial-JSON events and incorrect delimiter ordering when using the OpenAI compatibility layer and SDK streaming helpers. Motivation: several production incidents (SUP-2184) and internal canaries observed partial JSON fragments where the tokenizer/event boundary ordering resulted in out-of-order 'json' and 'delimiter' events, and tool/function-calling structured output could be split across SSE chunks resulting in invalid JSON for consumers. This PR standardizes event ordering, ensures token-level events are framed before delimiter tokens, and adds a small state machine to the SSE encoder to guarantee atomic 'partial_json' event boundaries when a structured output token crosses chunk boundaries. The change touches the SSE encoder/decoder, the OpenAI-compat streaming adapter, TypeScript SDK streaming glue, and adds unit + e2e streaming tests. The description below lists the change summary, testing notes, rollout plan, and compatibility considerations.
commits_summary: encoder: add framing state machine to guarantee token->event ordering
openai-compat: reorder events to emit 'json' payloads before delimiter tokens
sdk-ts: update streaming helper to buffer partial-json tokens until delimiter confirmed
tests: add deterministic fuzz for token/event ordering and partial-json boundary cases
docs: note streaming compatibility behavior and recommended SDK upgrade path
review_comments: Riley Morgan: Foundry tests caught a race where delimiter events could be emitted before buffered json tokens - good catch. Please add a fuzz test that exercises token splits at buffer boundaries.
Avery Chen: Added deterministic fuzz harness (encoder_test.go) that splits tokens at all byte offsets. Also added a state machine comment describing invariants.
Devon Patel: Can we keep backward compatibility for old SDKs that expect delimiter-first ordering? Any consumers relying on the previous ordering should be rare, but we need a migration note.

Avery Chen: Left a compatibility note in docs/streaming.md and added a small compatibility mode toggle in openai-compat that keeps old ordering for a single release window. Default is new safe ordering.
Elena Torres: CI flake in e2e-streaming on first run - re-ran and it passed. Approving after green.
Riley Morgan: LGTM. Please squash before merge and include release notes calling out the compatibility toggle.
merge_outcome: merged by squash via GitHub UI. Commit message: 'sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering & token/event framing (ENG-9421)'.
release_notes: Fixes: SSE streaming could emit delimiter events before buffered partial-JSON tokens which produced invalid JSON consumers could not parse. New behavior guarantees token->event framing and includes a compatibility toggle in openai-compat for one-release migration. Recommend upgrading SDKs (typescript 1.18.2) that include buffering changes. Impact: small rolling restart recommended for streaming adapters; no model changes required.
compatibility_and_rollout: Default behavior switches to safe framing ordering. A compatibility mode flag 'OPENAI_COMPAT_LEGACY_SSE_ORDER' is available for one release if customers need old ordering. Rolling restart of streaming adapters recommended; no client-side change required for updated SDKs but older SDKs may see parsing errors if not upgraded.
testing_notes: Added deterministic fuzz tests that split tokens at every possible byte boundary and assert reassembly invariants. Added integration e2e test that runs an OpenAI-compat streaming scenario with nested structured output (function/tool calling) and asserts valid JSON after reassembly. Verified canary passes in internal cluster.
notes_for_ops: When deploying, ensure canary set receives traffic first (10% for 30 minutes), watch streaming parse errors metric (streaming.parse_errors) and canary latency. If parse_errors spike with clients on older SDKs, enable compatibility toggle for that deployment group and notify affected customers.
changelog_summary: Bugfix: SSE streaming partial-JSON delimiter & token ordering - fixes malformed streaming JSON and improves stability for structured tool/function outputs in OpenAI-compat mode.
additional_context: Root cause: encoder used async flush path for delimiter tokens which could interleave with buffered token chunks produced by the tokenizer. The state machine ensures delimiters are only emitted after the corresponding token batch has been emitted or buffered until an explicit chunk boundary is observed. This reduces transient parse errors seen by long-lived streaming clients.
risk_and_mitigation: Low-medium risk: change is localized to streaming encoder and OpenAI-compat adapter. Mitigation: compatibility toggle, canary rollout, and additional observability on parse_errors and stream_reconnects.
manual_steps_after_merge: Deploy openai-compat service, set feature flag to default new ordering, monitor metrics; revert to legacy toggle if customers show failures.
estimated_impact: Fixes customer-facing streaming parse errors seen in ~0.2% of long-running streams during peak traffic; expected reduction of streaming.parse_errors by ~95% for affected workloads.
